description:
What is trending on podcasts: Particle's daily Trends charts, which rank the entities (people, shows, films, games, books, brands, athletes, teams) that the most podcasts are talking about, with each entry's movement since the previous edition and, when the editors explained it, why it moved, backed by a verbatim podcast quote and a link that plays it.

Call with no arguments for the cross-category `all` chart. Pick a narrower chart with `chart` (its schema lists every chart and the windows it publishes): entertainment (`tv-series`, `movies`, `video-games`), sports leagues (`nfl`, `nba`, ...), books (`fiction`, `nonfiction`, `comics-manga`), and `guests`, which ranks people by the distinct shows they appeared on. `sort=acceleration` surfaces the fastest risers anywhere in the chart.

Rank does not always follow the podcast count: most charts weigh how far an entry's coverage sits above its own normal level, so a lower count can rank higher.

Each entry returns a slug. Pass an entity slug to `particle_entity_get`, or to `particle_podcast_get_mention_trends` (`entity_slug`) for which podcasts drive it; pass a person slug to `particle_person_get` or `particle_podcast_get_guest`; pass a quote's episode id to `particle_podcast_get_episode`.

Not for podcast shows' own chart positions on Apple or Spotify: use `particle_podcast_get_rankings`. Not for one subject you already know: use `particle_podcast_get_mention_trends`.

chart.description:
Which chart to read. Defaults to 'all'. The charts, with their group and the windows each publishes:
'all-entertainment': All Entertainment (entertainment; 7d)
'tv-series': TV Series (entertainment; 7d, 24h)
'movies': Movies (entertainment; 7d, 24h)
'video-games': Video Games (entertainment; 7d, 24h)
'guests': Guest Appearances (overall; 7d, 24h)
'all': All Entities (overall; 7d)
'all-sports': All Sports (sports; 7d)
'nfl': NFL (sports; 7d, 24h)
'nba': NBA (sports; 7d, 24h)
'mlb': MLB (sports; 7d, 24h)
'nhl': NHL (sports; 7d, 24h)
'college-football': College Football (sports; 7d, 24h)
'wnba': WNBA (sports; 7d)
'college-basketball': College Basketball (sports; 7d)
'soccer': Soccer (sports; 7d)
'golf': Golf (sports; 7d)
'tennis': Tennis (sports; 7d)
'formula-1': Formula 1 (sports; 7d)
'nascar': NASCAR (sports; 7d)
'pro-wrestling': Pro Wrestling (sports; 7d)
'fiction': Fiction (books; 7d)
'comics-manga': Comics & Manga (books; 7d)
'nonfiction': Non-Fiction (books; 7d)

include.description: Optional sections. 'timeseries' adds each entry's daily podcast and mention counts. 'driven_by' names, on an entry that rises because of another entry's coverage (a song with its artist), the entry that drives it.

limit.description: How many ranked entries to return, from rank 1 down (1-100, default 10).

output_format.description: Output serialization. 'markdown' (default) returns the LLM-facing rendering. 'json' returns the structured payload as JSON text — use only for programmatic chaining where exact field extraction matters; the JSON shape is larger and noisier for an LLM to read.

sort.description: 'rank' (default): the chart as published. 'acceleration': the whole edition reordered by how fast each entry's coverage is growing, fastest first, so a fast riser deep in the chart surfaces; each entry keeps its published rank. Not measured on the guests chart, which stays in rank order.

window.description: Measurement window. '7d' (default) ranks the last seven days; '24h' ranks the last day. The composite charts and most sports charts publish 7d only (see chart).

name: particle_podcast_get_entity_chart
title: Particle Podcast Get Entity Chart
